subject: AtlasPay reserved throughput deficit & tail latency — urgent mitigation and exec sync
messages:
From: Jessica Tran <jessica@atlaspay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasPay SRE <sre@atlaspay.com>
Date: 2028-05-07T08:12:04Z
Subject: Production: spike in tail latency + 429s on reserved capacity — urgent

Laura —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a sustained ~4–6% 429 rate on our production routes that use the reserved capacity. This started around 06:30 UTC and has persisted despite retry attempts. Our telemetry shows saturated GPU utilization on the dedicated pool and a measurable drop in achieved tokens/sec versus our committed throughput.

Attached: atlas_qps_metrics_may7.csv (QPS + 429/latency by minute).

This is impacting checkout flows — several transactions are failing or retrying which is causing downstream payment timeouts. Our SREs are standing by on the bridge (sre@atlaspay.com). We need Redwood to investigate immediately:
- Confirm whether reserved capacity throttling is occurring on your side
- Provide immediate mitigation steps and ETA for traffic normalization

Happy to join a quick bridge.

— Jessica
Jessica Tran
Head of SRE, AtlasPay

Subject: Re: Production: spike in tail latency + 429s on reserved capacity — urgent

Jessica — thanks for the heads-up and the metrics. We're pulling the on-call ops team onto a bridge now. I'm copying Dylan (runtime), Grace (CS), and Marissa (AM) — we'll coordinate with Atlas SRE.

Immediate next steps (we're executing now):
- Open bridge and collect span ids + sample requests
- Inspect reserved pool headroom and active queue depth
- If pools are saturated, we will enable temporary burst capacity and route lower-priority traffic to a fallback model variant

I've attached a short runbook we'll follow for rapid mitigation (short_runbook.txt). I'll post updates to this thread and keep you in the loop. Can you confirm the most impacted route names and any span ids you captured?

— Laura

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-07T09:05:43Z
Subject: Re: Production: spike in tail latency + 429s on reserved capacity — urgent (ops findings)

On Tue, May 7, 2028 at 08:12 AM Jessica Tran <jessica@atlaspay.com> wrote:
> Laura —
>
> We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a sustained ~4–6% 429 rate on our production routes that use the reserved capacity. ...

Quick ops note after initial triage:
- Observed: 3 of 12 GPUs in AtlasPay's dedicated pool are at 98–100% sustained utilization for ~40m; queue depth for the pool increased 7x relative to baseline.
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden burst of high-concurrency requests hitting long-context endpoints triggered KV cache misses and larger per-request memory working sets. This increased per-request latency and reduced effective throughput, causing our admission controller to start returning 429-like throttles for some routes.
- Evidence: attached server-side sample logs (excerpt below):
  [2028-05-07T08:01:23Z] pool=atlas-dedicated-3 gpu0=99% queue=142 wait_ms=1200
  [2028-05-07T08:06:12Z] pool=atlas-dedicated-3 gpu0=100% queue=198 wait_ms=1800

Short-term actions executed (08:35–09:00 UTC):
- Enabled reserved pool burst capacity + brought two warm standby nodes online (temporary)
- De-prioritized background batch workloads routed to the same pool
- Reduced per-request batching window (drops latency at cost of some token efficiency)
- Began routing 15% of traffic to a smaller, lower-latency model variant as a graceful fallback

Immediate ask for Atlas SRE: provide any recent change that might have increased request concurrency (rollout, feature flags, client retries).

We'll continue monitoring; I expect visible improvement within 20–30 minutes of the routing change.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production: spike in tail latency + 429s on reserved capacity — commercial note

Jessica —

Thanks for flagging this. From a commercial perspective I want to be transparent about options and next steps:
- If the mitigation above is not sufficient, we can immediately provision additional reserved headroom for the remainder of the billing cycle and evaluate a short-term usage credit while we steady the pool.
- We'll also need to check the SLA attachment (excerpt attached) to align on any credit calculation (contract_sla_excerpt.pdf).

Can we schedule a 30-minute exec readout for later today if the issue persists? Laura and I can join; if this is hitting revenue/checkout impact materially, I'll prep a commercial remediation proposal.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Tran <jessica@atlaspay.com>, AtlasPay SRE <sre@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-07T12:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: spike in tail latency + 429s on reserved capacity — mitigation update

Jessica / SRE team —

Quick update from the bridge:
- Actions taken: enabled burst capacity, spun up 2 warm nodes, reduced batching window, routed 15% traffic to fallback model variant.
- Outcome (11:45 UTC): 429 rate down from ~5% to ~0.4%; 95th tail latency improved by ~480ms. See attached post_mitigation_qps.csv for minute-level numbers.
- Next steps: keep mitigation in place for 2–4 hours while we (a) continue to monitor for relapse, (b) analyze cache warm-up behavior, and (c) run a controlled canary for the fallback model at slightly higher traffic share if stable.

We're continuing a root cause post-mortem to determine whether a permanent capacity increase (or policy tweak to admission control) is warranted. I'll follow up with a summary and recommended next steps once we have the full trace-sample analysis.

Please reply on this thread with any additional logs or anomalies you see.

— Laura
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-07T18:15:22Z
Subject: Exec: AtlasPay saturation event — request for readout and commercial guidance

Team —

Why you're seeing this note: AtlasPay (AP-DEAL-7890) experienced a reserved-capacity saturation event this morning that produced elevated 429s and tail latency for ~90 minutes. Customer impact: checkout latency spikes and a small but material increase in failed transactions while the pool was saturated.

Summary (high-level):
- Timeline: first signal 06:30 UTC; mitigations executed 08:35–09:00 UTC; normalizing by ~11:45 UTC.
- Measured impact: peak 429 rate ~5%, sustained queue increases on 3/12 GPUs, 95th latency delta +480ms during peak.
- Actions taken: enabled burst capacity, spun warm nodes, decreased batching, routed 15% to lower-latency model. Post-mitigation metrics show a >90% reduction in 429s.

Open asks for executive guidance:
1) Commercial: recommend offering a one-time usage credit for the impacted billing period while we finalize root cause and longer-term remediation. Marissa can draft numbers; I want sign-off to propose to Atlas.
2) Capacity policy: propose increasing the reserved pool buffer for AtlasPay by +20% (commit/price TBD) or alternatively introduce auto-burst with guaranteed min headroom for enterprise customers.
3) Communication: approve a short exec readout to AtlasPay leadership tonight (30-min) to confirm mitigations and next steps.

Attached: draft_mitigation_plan.pdf and links to the daily bridge notes: https://redwood.internal/ops/bridges/BR-4521 and HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/deal/AP-DEAL-7890

Please advise on the commercial ask (#1) and whether you want me to set the readout for 19:30 UTC.

— Laura
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
